why: musl fmemopen (0x96a1c) calls the malloc trampoline 0x540cc at +0x98 (0x96ab4, return 0x96ab8) and +0xa8 (0x96ac4, return 0x96ac8). The composer does not walk it: it is reached mark_quietly 0x88410 -> __interceptor_trampoline_fmemopen 0x430a8 (j, below main, so outside the composer's region) -> ___interceptor_fmemopen 0x48024 (restores s0 at 0x48060, then jr t1 at 0x48070; t1 = the word at 0xa3780, __interception::real_fmemopen in .data, = 0x96a1c in the image; the only instruction that names 0xa3780 is that load 0x4804c, and no data word holds 0xa3780) -> fmemopen (s0 first written at 0x96acc, after both calls). So s0 at both calls is mark_quietly's s0, which mark_quietly sets to its a1 at 0x883e8 (it keeps no frame record): 0 or 0x20fc0 at the call 0x831f8, and 0, 0x62fac0 + 8k (k <= 0x3f) or a word of the read-only table 0xa1760 (0x20fc0..0x21060) at the call 0x8347c (decide.link.json 0x8841c). Each is 0 or an image address below the stack, so the walk ends at the call. The +0xa8 call needs buf = NULL; mark_quietly passes the .bss address 0x62fee0 (0x883fc auipc + 0x88404 addi) as buf, so the harness never makes it; it is listed as the donor lists its never-made calls.
